blocks.h: Questions validation, QA and IT teams ask

items.q: How can our QA team check your controls without a prior audit record?
items.a: Before you order, review the sample FAT protocol and turnover package, the functional and design specifications and the traceability matrix from each requirement to its test. Your QA team can audit [our software development and change control procedure] and witness the controls FAT.

items.q: Do we get full access to the PLC and HMI code?
items.a: [code delivered unlocked, and who owns it] The software version and checksum seen at FAT are recorded, so you can show an inspector that the code running is the code that was tested.

items.q: How do you test the controls at FAT before shipment?
items.a: Every input and output is checked, every sequence, alarm and interlock is run on water, and audit trail entries, user access levels and recovery after a power failure are tested against the functional specification. The FAT and SAT page lists what IQ/OQ can leverage.

items.q: Can we release water on online TOC and conductivity?
items.a: Yes, for those two attributes, when the instruments are qualified, the sample point represents the water used and your procedures say so. Online conductivity covers stage 1 only; a failure goes to stages 2 and 3 in the laboratory. Microbial counts and, for WFI, endotoxin stay laboratory tests unless you qualify an alternative method.

items.q: Our transmitters show temperature-compensated conductivity. Is that a problem?
items.a: For trending, no. USP <645> stage 1 uses the uncompensated reading against the table row for the measured temperature, rounded down: 23.8 °C uses 20 °C, 1.1 µS/cm; 67 °C uses 65 °C, 2.4 µS/cm; 82 °C uses 80 °C, 2.7 µS/cm. Compensation can pass water stage 1 would fail, or the reverse. We store both, labelled.

items.q: Is your system Part 11 compliant, and who validates it?
items.a: No system is compliant on its own; your site is, by technical controls plus procedures. We supply the controls and a Part 11 and Annex 11 assessment showing which need a site procedure. Your validation team owns the computerized system validation; FAT records can be leveraged in OQ if your procedures allow and protocols are approved first.

items.q: Can you fix controls on an existing system from another builder?
items.a: Yes. We start with a gap assessment against Part 11, Annex 11 and USP <645>: shared logins, missing audit trail, compensated-only conductivity, unsynchronized clocks, paper recorders. The upgrade is scoped to the gaps, with cut-over and requalification agreed with your quality unit first. See upgrades and requalification.

items.q: Our IT team allows no remote access to GMP equipment.
items.a: Then we do not install it. The system runs and records fully without any outside connection. If you later allow read-only telemetry or supervised sessions, they connect through your DMZ under your IT and change control, with every session logged.
